testProviders.name: GL Assessment
testProviders.description: Commercial assessment publisher. Produces the Buckinghamshire Secondary Transfer Test for The Buckinghamshire Grammar Schools.

testProviders.name: Consortium of Selective Schools in Essex (CSSE)
testProviders.description: Administers the 11+ examination on behalf of its member schools in Essex and Southend-on-Sea.
testProviders.locator: "The CSSE Office administers the 11+ Examination on behalf of the CSSE Member schools."

testProviders.name: Schools' Entrance Assessment Group (SEAG)
testProviders.description: Runs the SEAG Entrance Assessment used by Northern Ireland post-primary schools that admit pupils on the basis of academic selection.

entranceTests.name: Buckinghamshire Secondary Transfer Test
entranceTests.administeredBy: Buckinghamshire Council on behalf of The Buckinghamshire Grammar Schools
entranceTests.areaDescription: The thirteen state grammar schools in Buckinghamshire.

components.subject: Mathematical and non-verbal skills
components.detail: The other paper assesses mathematical and non-verbal skills.

entranceTests.format: Two test papers, each approximately 60 minutes, taken on the same day in the autumn term of Year 6.
entranceTests.standardisation: Scores in the three skill areas are age-standardised and added together to give the Secondary Transfer Test Score (STTS) (Aylesbury Grammar School admissions policy 2027, 3.2).
entranceTests.scoreScale: Secondary Transfer Test Score (STTS). A score of 121 or above automatically qualifies a child for consideration.
entranceTests.summary: Children who attend Buckinghamshire state primary schools are registered automatically unless a parent opts out; others must register with Buckinghamshire Council. A standardised score of 121 or above qualifies a child for consideration; children below 121 can apply for a Selection Review.
entranceTests.schoolLinkNote: TBGS states the Secondary Transfer Test selects pupils for the thirteen Buckinghamshire grammar schools; these are the thirteen state grammar schools in Buckinghamshire in GIAS.

entranceTests.name: CSSE 11+ Examination
entranceTests.administeredBy: CSSE Office, on behalf of member schools
entranceTests.areaDescription: CSSE member schools in Essex and Southend-on-Sea.

components.subject: English
components.detail: 60 minutes, plus ten minutes of additional reading time.

entranceTests.scoreScale: Not stated on the CSSE home page. Each member school's admissions policy sets how scores are used.
entranceTests.summary: CSSE administers one 11+ examination for its member schools. Registration for 2028 entry opens in May 2027. How scores are used differs by school: always check each school's admissions policy.
entranceTests.locator: Home page — CSSE 11+ Examination and CSSE Members
entranceTests.schoolLinkNote: Schools listed as CSSE member schools on csse.org.uk.

entranceTests.name: SEAG Entrance Assessment
entranceTests.areaDescription: Northern Ireland post-primary schools that use academic selection.

components.subject: English (or Gaeilge)
components.detail: 28 questions in the Main Test of each paper.

components.subject: Mathematics
components.detail: 28 questions in the Main Test of each paper.

entranceTests.format: Two papers with an identical format, set at the same level of difficulty. Each has an untimed practice test and a 60-minute main test.
entranceTests.standardisation: Outcomes are standardised to take account of the pupil's age when they took the assessment.
entranceTests.scoreScale: Statement of Outcomes: a Band from 1 (highest) to 6 (lowest), a Total Standardised Age Score (English/Gaeilge SAS + Mathematics SAS), and a cohort percentile.
entranceTests.summary: Taken by pupils in their final year of primary school (P7) who will transfer to post-primary school the following September. Each school publishes its own admissions criteria, which say how SEAG outcomes are used.
entranceTests.schoolLinkNote: School-by-school use of SEAG must be confirmed from each school's published admissions criteria.

entranceTests.name: The Kent Test
entranceTests.areaDescription: The Kent grammar schools listed in Kent County Council's co-ordinated scheme for secondary admissions.
entranceTests.summary: Kent County Council's grammar school assessment. For September 2027 entry, registration ran from 1 June to 1 July 2026; the test was on 10 September 2026 for pupils at Kent primary schools and the weekend of 12 and 13 September for others, with decisions sent on 15 October 2026. A Grammar assessment does not guarantee a place: each school applies its own oversubscription criteria. Some schools also accept their own test.
entranceTests.locator: Paragraph 13 (schools requiring the Kent Grammar school assessment) and the Key Scheme dates table
entranceTests.schoolLinkNote: Listed in paragraph 13 of Kent County Council's co-ordinated scheme for 2027/28. Borden, Dover Grammar School for Boys, Dover Grammar School for Girls, The Folkestone School for Girls, The Harvey Grammar School, Highsted and Mayfield also accept pupils who reach the standard in their own school test.

entranceTests.name: The Medway Test
entranceTests.format: Three papers, with at least a 20-minute break between them, sat at a Medway Council venue in Medway.
entranceTests.summary: Medway Council's 11+. Children must sit it to be considered for a Medway grammar school, wherever they live. Passing does not guarantee a place: oversubscribed schools apply their own criteria.
entranceTests.locator: "If you would like your child to be considered for a Medway grammar school they will need to sit the Medway Test"; "Our test provider is GL Assessment."
entranceTests.schoolLinkNote: Medway Council states children need the Medway Test to be considered for a Medway grammar school. Chatham Grammar also accepts the Kent Test.

entranceTests.name: Lincolnshire Consortium 11+
entranceTests.areaDescription: Member grammar schools of the Lincolnshire Consortium.
entranceTests.format: A verbal reasoning test and a non-verbal reasoning test, answered on optical mark reading sheets.
entranceTests.scoreScale: Qualification is an aggregate standardised score of 220, set to identify the most able 25% of pupils in Lincolnshire's selective areas.
entranceTests.summary: The shared 11+ used by most Lincolnshire grammar schools, provided by GL Assessment. Reaching the qualifying score does not by itself guarantee admission to any school.
entranceTests.locator: "The Lincolnshire Consortium of Grammar Schools currently uses GL Assessment to provide 11+ Testing"; "Qualification represents a score of 220"
entranceTests.schoolLinkNote: Listed as a school where pupils completed the consortium test papers in 2026 (consortium site, 2026 Completed papers by schools). Confirm membership against each school's admission arrangements.

entranceTests.name: West Midlands shared 11+ test
entranceTests.administeredBy: Shared by the grammar schools of Warwickshire, Birmingham, Walsall, Wolverhampton and Shropshire
entranceTests.areaDescription: Grammar schools in Warwickshire, Birmingham, Walsall and Wolverhampton (and Shropshire).
entranceTests.summary: One set of 11+ papers used across several West Midlands areas. Candidates can choose to have their result shared with every area if they plan to apply to grammar schools in more than one. For September 2027 entry the Warwickshire test dates were 12 and 13 September 2026.
entranceTests.locator: "The 11+ test is currently operated as a shared test between the Warwickshire, Birmingham, Walsall, Wolverhampton and Shropshire Grammar Schools. The same test papers are used across all authorities"
entranceTests.schoolLinkNote: Warwickshire County Council states the 11+ is a shared test across the Warwickshire, Birmingham, Walsall, Wolverhampton and Shropshire grammar schools. Warwickshire schools are named on the council's 'Grammar schools in Warwickshire' page; for Birmingham, Walsall and Wolverhampton, confirm against each school's admission arrangements. The two Newport schools (Telford and Wrekin) are not linked because 'Shropshire' is not specific enough.

entranceTests.name: Bexley Selection Test
entranceTests.areaDescription: The four grammar schools in Bexley.

components.subject: Numerical reasoning
components.detail: Content not beyond what children are expected to learn by the end of Year 5.

entranceTests.format: Two papers taken in the same session, each about 50 minutes plus time for instructions.
entranceTests.scoreScale: A selective test mark decided by the grammar school head teachers.
entranceTests.summary: A single test for admission to all four Bexley grammar schools. Families must register online, including children at Bexley primary schools. Reaching the selective standard does not guarantee a place.
entranceTests.locator: Section 4: "Bexley has 4 Grammar Schools"; "a single test is used for admission to all four grammar schools"
entranceTests.schoolLinkNote: Named by the London Borough of Bexley as one of the four grammar schools using the single Bexley Selection Test.

entranceTests.name: Sutton Selective Eligibility Test (SET)
entranceTests.areaDescription: Greenshaw High School and the five Sutton grammar schools.
entranceTests.format: A first-stage eligibility test. Grammar schools then hold their own second-stage test for those who pass (girls at Nonsuch or Wallington High School for Girls, with a joint test).
entranceTests.summary: A shared first-stage test. Passing the SET makes a child eligible for a school's second stage; it is not an offer of a place.
entranceTests.locator: "The 'participating schools' in the Selective Eligibility Test, 'SET', are Greenshaw High School, Nonsuch High School for Girls, Sutton Grammar School, Wallington County Grammar School, Wallington High School for Girls and Wilson's School."
entranceTests.schoolLinkNote: Named as a participating school in the Sutton Selective Eligibility Test in Sutton Grammar School's admissions FAQs.

entranceTests.name: Slough Consortium of Grammar Schools 11+
entranceTests.summary: One test, registered for once, to assess eligibility for any of the four Slough grammar schools. The consortium contracts GL Assessment as its test provider; its tests differ from other areas' GL tests.
entranceTests.locator: "Children take one test to assess their eligibility for any of the four Slough grammar schools"; "The Slough Consortium has its own contract with GL Assessment as the test provider"; planned admission numbers list the four schools
entranceTests.schoolLinkNote: Named in the Slough Consortium's September 2027 admissions briefing as one of the four Slough grammar schools sharing the test.

entranceTests.name: Gloucestershire Grammar Schools' Entrance Test
entranceTests.areaDescription: The seven grammar schools in Gloucestershire.
entranceTests.format: Two papers of about 45 to 50 minutes each, sat on the same day with a short break, answered on separate sheets that are marked electronically by an independent company.
entranceTests.summary: The same entrance test for all seven Gloucestershire grammar schools, sat on the same day. For September 2027 entry the provider was GL Assessment (per Pate's Grammar School); the schools have appointed a new provider from 2028 entry.
entranceTests.locator: Section 1, table of the seven grammar schools; Section 2: "The Entrance Tests are the same for all seven grammar schools in Gloucestershire and are sat on the same day."
entranceTests.schoolLinkNote: Listed in the Gloucestershire Grammar Schools' admissions information for September 2027 as one of the seven schools sharing the entrance test.

policies.document: Aylesbury Grammar School Admissions Policy 2027 (determined 5 December 2025)
policies.summary: Boys qualify by achieving a Secondary Transfer Test Score of 121 or more, or by being deemed qualified at a Selection Review. If more qualified boys apply than there are places, looked after and previously looked after boys come first. Up to 6 places then go to catchment-area boys eligible for Pupil Premium who scored 115–120. After that come catchment Pupil Premium boys, siblings, staff children, medical or social need and other catchment-area boys. All other qualified boys come last. Within each category, boys living closer to the school are offered places first.
policies.qualificationSummary: Secondary Transfer Test Score (STTS) of 121 or more, or deemed qualified by a Selection Review (or, exceptionally, an admissions appeal). Up to 6 places are available to looked after/previously looked after boys and catchment-area boys eligible for Pupil Premium who score 115–120.
policies.catchmentSummary: The school has a defined catchment area. A map is published on the school's website, and Buckinghamshire Council provides a catchment checker by postcode. Residence counts from 1 September of the year before entry and must be continuous.
policies.distanceMethod: Straight-line distance from the child's home address to the middle of the school's main entrance gate on Walton Road. The home point is taken from Ordnance Survey ADDRESS-POINT.
policies.tieBreak: Distance (closest first). Where two applicants live exactly the same distance away, random selection supervised by a person independent of the school.
policies.waitingList: Buckinghamshire Council manages waiting lists for Years 7–9 for qualifying applicants, ranked by the oversubscription criteria (not by date added). Test qualification remains current until the end of Year 9.
policies.appeals: Parents can appeal to an Independent Appeal Panel. The school has contracted Buckinghamshire Council to manage appeals. An appeal panel will not ordinarily re-review whether a boy could have qualified — that is the role of the Selection Review.
policies.addressRules: Home address is where the boy lives and sleeps more than 50% of Sunday–Thursday nights in term time. To count as resident in catchment for the 1 March allocation, families should have disposed of any previous property by 1 September of the preceding year.
policies.inYearAdmissions: Admission other than into Year 7 via the Secondary Transfer Test follows the school's Late Transfer Procedure (tests coordinated by Buckinghamshire Council for Years 7–9; school-set English and maths tests for Years 10–11).

scoreRules.description: Boys are eligible to be considered for admission if they meet the qualifying score of 121, or have been deemed qualified by a Selection Review.

scoreRules.scoreScale: Buckinghamshire Secondary Transfer Test Score (STTS), 115 to 120 inclusive
scoreRules.description: Up to 6 places for looked after or previously looked after boys living anywhere, or catchment-area boys eligible for Pupil Premium, who score 115 to 120 inclusive and have not been deemed qualified by Selection Review.

criteria.title: Looked after and previously looked after boys
Up to 6 places: looked after/previously looked after boys, or catchment-area boys eligible for Pupil Premium, scoring 115–120
criteria.description: Applies to boys scoring 115–120 who have not been deemed qualified by Selection Review. Within this category, looked after children are prioritised.

criteria.title: Catchment-area boys eligible for Pupil Premium
Siblings of boys on roll at Aylesbury Grammar School at the date of entry
Siblings of girls on roll at Aylesbury High School at the date of entry
Siblings of boys who have previously been on roll at Aylesbury Grammar School
Children of eligible Aylesbury Grammar School staff
criteria.description: Staff on a permanent contract for at least two years at the time of application, or recruited to fill a post with a demonstrable skills shortage.

criteria.title: Exceptional medical or social needs that can only be met at the school
criteria.description: Must be supported by written evidence from a doctor, social worker, educational welfare officer or other appropriately qualified person.

criteria.title: Boys living in the catchment area
criteria.description: Living in the catchment area as at and continuously from 1 September of the year before entry.
